Celebrate Uniqueness
Welcome to The Windmill School
We are a special free school managed by Barnet Special Education Trust. When full, we shall provide 90 places for pupils between the ages of 5 and 19, who, because of their autism, experience of burnout, this significantly impacts their capacity to learn successfully in mainstream or generic special school environments.
A fundamental principle underpinning all provision at The Windmill School is the celebration of neurodiversity. We recognise and value the unique strengths, interests, and characteristics of every pupil and are committed to ensuring that each young person is understood, respected, and supported to thrive as their authentic self.
In the 2025-26 academy year we were funded for 70 places, based at our new permanent home on Moxon Street, High Barnet, which opened in April 2024. I am very proud to be the first headteacher of this brand new specialist autism school and I hope that you find the information you are looking for on this site. If you wish to visit our school in person, please contact us, as we welcome visitors throughout the year. However we are very oversubscribed with huge demand for places, and very close to full capacity with 86 pupils; we are therefore only prioritising requests for phased transfer Year 6-Year 7 in the academic year 2026-2027.
GINNY D'ODORICO MSc NPQH | HEADTEACHER

Connecting Steps

Values & Ethos
Many of our pupils may have masked abilities in their former school setting or indeed since early childhood, as more complex social demands begin to exceed abilities or coping strategies. Our pupils may have developed an increasing recognition of difference in terms of their peers’ abilities, interests, and characteristic personalities. It is likely pupils may recognise qualitative differences between themselves and non-autistic peers which may contribute to secondary mental health difficulties associated with low self-esteem and anxiety.
Whilst the Windmill School offers a supportive, compassionate, and responsive environment we acknowledge the range of compensatory and adjustment strategies our pupils may have developed that may impact them negatively in terms of their sense of self.
A unique pedagogy for autism
All our pedagogy and teaching methodology offer opportunities for self-expression and self-exploration achieved through the curriculum and particularly through the arts such as music, poetry, writing fiction, drawing sculpture, textiles, and dance. We find our pupils will traverse into deeper and broader learning experiences following a period of learning they find energising where their abilities are embraced, and their passions appreciated.
Our Trust-Wide Vision
Celebrate Uniqueness
Children and young people with a unique profile require the autism specific environment that the Windmill School will offer. The school was developed to engage and motivate all pupils by providing a curriculum that relates to them as individuals.
Central to our work is the concept that we want to avoid separation and exclusion and ensure inclusion is the core. Our key message is to not generalise teaching approaches but respond to the learning needs of each Windmill pupil as an individual.
Many of our young people like to ‘figure things out by themselves’ once equipped with knowledge of the world that is presented in a motivating and engaging way. We give high regard to the environment where all our pupils have control over their physical learning environment; this reduces social anxiety, therefore, enables access to learning. Our philosophy and ethos is important for the following reasons:
Autistic pupils need evidence-informed approaches including quality-first teaching and practice to remove barriers and allow them to learn effectively inside and outside the classroom.
Educating autistic pupils benefits from a whole-child approach, recognizing that attention to pupils’ mental health and emotional well-being is just as important as their autism.
Innovative and individualized methods of adapting the curriculum, utilizing pupils’ strengths and interests, are essential for ensuring that it is accessible, effective and engaging for pupils.
Close working relationships with parents, recognizing their key role, expertise and joint decision making, as well as their need for support, is essential for ensuring that learning continues outside the school.
Autistic pupils who are engaged in their learning, and who are active participants in decisions about their learning, are more likely to be confident learners in the short- term and the longer term.

Welcome
The Windmill School opened in September 2023 as an all age special free school for up to 90 pupils aged 5-19 with a primary diagnosis of autism. It has been developed by senior leaders from Oak Lodge School in East Finchley, building on their skills and experience in autism education and supported by a team of specialist academics and education consultants including autistic scholars.
The language used to describe autism is currently the subject of intense discussion. All content on our website includes identity first language (e.g., autistic person’) so that we are respectful to those on the autism spectrum their families and supporters. Universally used langauge across all policy and in the school community promotes a truly inclusive and neurodiversity-affirmative mindset.
The Windmill School complements the existing range of generic special schools and autism specific provisions in mainstream schools, to offer places for children who, because of their autistic profile, find the sensory aspects of those environments too challenging for successful progress in their learning.
We have strong links with IOE Centre for Research in Autism and Education as the Headteacher has strong links with research and academics in autism and education. Therefore our attention to real world autism research that is directly applicable in the classroom with a positive impact on outcomes has enabled us to design and implement a specialist curriculum.
Testimonials from our research collaborators
Being autistic in a world run by non-autistic people is never going to be straightforward. Windmill responds to this reality by providing an educational environment shaped by research and deeply responsive to the lived experiences of Autistic young people.
This is achieved by ensuring that knowledge about the world is presented in motivating and engaging ways, empowering pupils to figure things out for themselves.
By ensuring that Autistic pupils are genuinely cared for, with close attention to their individual needs, mental health, and emotional wellbeing.
And by ensuring that Autistic pupils are given multiple opportunities to be active participants in decisions about their learning, setting them up to shape their own paths in life.
This is what Windmill offers: a place where Autistic young people can flourish.
(Liz Pellicano, Professor of Autism Research, University College London)
Ginny D’Odorico’s leadership of The Windmill School is genuinely visionary. She has created an educational environment that is not only deeply informed by the latest and most rigorous research but is also - crucially - shaped by the lived experiences, perspectives, and priorities of autistic people themselves. This combination is rare and powerful. It ensures that practice at Windmill is both evidence-based and meaningfully grounded in the realities of autistic young people’s lives.
The young people at The Windmill and their families are exceptionally fortunate to be part of a school led with such clarity of purpose and commitment to inclusion.
Under Ginny’s outstanding leadership, Windmill is setting a standard for what autism-informed education can and should be.
Professor Laura Crane, Director of the Autism Centre for Education and Research (ACER), University of Birmingham

Parent Partnership
At the Windmill School all our pedagogy and practice is underpinned by the SCERTS Model a family centred approach to prioritising needs that arise for autistic children and young people. Together we work with parents to address core goals that enhance social emotional development and promote active engagement with learning.
Emily Rubin one of the co-authors of the SCERTS Model has been a collaborator with The Windmill School since opening. Emily has run parent workshops here at Windmill and more recently hosted a webinar for the IOE_UCL Centre for Research in Autism and Education.
//www.youtube.com/embed/pDBSO1Ud1OU#t=0.5
The Social Communication Emotional Regulation Transactional Support (SCERTS) Model helps families, teachers and therapists work cooperatively to support our students.
We firmly believe that when parents are partners in their child's school life they can play an active role in extending that support at home. Consistency of approach across home and school is essential for developing emotional self regulation.
We have seen how pupils thrive at school when we focus on building family-centred partnerships that are built on trust. Barry Prizant author of SCERTS states firmly 'Parent professional relationships ' its a matter of trust"
We run autism informed training both face to face and online for parents.

We encourage frequent contact to help parents, carers and staff ensure consistency in response to certain events or behaviours. This helps to make life seem more predictable and safe for many pupils and supports them to learn well and make good progress.
The Barnet Council's Local Offer is also available to support families and schools.
In addition to Parental Consultation Evenings and the more formal Annual Review meeting, contact may take the form of a home/school book, regular informal telephone conversations or regular email.
Parents are of course welcome to come into the school, by appointment, at any time.
Christine is a parent counsellor employed by the Barnet Special Education Trust. Christines work therefore extends to provide counselling to parents at The Windmill School. Referrals are made by Elham Seyadi-Yazdi Deputy Headteacher with a responsibility for Pastoral Mental Health and Well-Being and Therapeutic Support. Referrals may be made at parents request. Christine jointly runs a parent/ carer group with Elham, however her individual parent clients she sees separately, often at her office on the Oak Lodge school site. Christine may help with a range of parental requirements that fall under her remit as parent liaison, including completing forms for DLA and PIP claims.
There are often other opportunities for parents to be involved in the life of the school: helping on your child's school trip, coffee mornings, workshops or other special events. Please check the Parent Noticeboard, or see our news posts for the latest information.

MOON Partnership
As part of an ongoing strategy of school led self-improvement, The Windmill School works in partnership with other special schools and academies in Barnet.
Within the partnership, schools work together to support each other and share best practice.
Collectively we are known as the MOON Partnership. The four original schools of the partnership have now welcomed Kisharon, Oak Hill and The Windmill Schools to this growing network of mutual support.

Care & Wellbeing
The welfare of your son or daughter is important to everyone at The Windmill School. Our circle of support will ensure that your child receives the care needed to develop to the best of his or her ability.
Our classroom teams aim to provide an environment where each pupil is able to feel safe and cared for. However, we understand that there may always be a time where a child or young person may need further support to thrive successfully in school. We have a well-developed and Trust-wide multi-disciplinary pastoral team, who are all here to help when needed.
If at any point you feel that extra support may be needed and there are issues that you wish to discuss with any member of staff please email or telephone the school to make an appointment.

Safeguarding
Child protection is an integrated part of the ethos and practices of our school. Our pupils, by default of having an Educational Health and Care Plan are children in need.
The Windmill School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of its children and young people and expects all staff, agency staff, volunteers and visitors to share the same commitment.
All staff attend regular safeguarding training provided by external agencies and are kept up to date with legislation changes by our Designated Safeguarding Lead, Elham Seyedi-Yazdi. This is supported through online safeguarding training programmes, which are a compulsory requirement for all staff working directly with students.
The Headteacher is the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) however there are also 2 members of the teaching staff who are deputy DSL's. A trained DSL will be on site at all times.
Paul Wardrop-Day Assistant Headteacher DSL
Where staff have a concern about a child they follow the processes outlined in the schools Child Protection Policy, this includes making a report via CPOMS which is a safeguarding and child protection management system for schools.
Every member of the school staff team has an obligation to report any concerns they may have. Once information is logged into the central system an alert is sent to the DSL and deputy DSL so that a chronology is build around that pupil and can be used to produce reports for OFSTED and school Governors. CPOMS is not a replacement for immediately passing on a child protection concern to a Designated Safeguarding Lead.
All school staff are required to read Part 1 of Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), in each year that it is published, to ensure they understand their responsibilities.
Under no circumstances will a volunteer who has not been checked be left unsupervised or allowed to work in regulated activity. We use the Disclosure and Barring Service DBS standard and enhanced ID checks for all staff employed. When recruiting new staff we follow the 'Safer Recruitment' processes including as appropriate relevant sections of KCSIE (2023).
We view school as a protective factor in a child or young persons life and attendance is a high priority.
We work with all teams around each child to ensure any circumstances that prevent a child from attending school are quickly addressed.
Online Safety and Cyber Security are given an exceptionally high priority in our school. Autistic young people are often straightforward, and they may not always grasp easily that not everything is to be trusted on the internet. Whilst this is a huge advantage (due to their honesty) nonetheless, our pupils may be vulnerable. It is very important to teach an autistic child that not everyone is as sincere as they are and protect them from the plethora of information on the world wide web. See our section on E-Safety for parents for more information.

MP Dan Tomlinson
Dan Tomlinson MP hosts SEND roundtable discussion with local Chipping Barnet Headteachers at The Windmill School
The Windmill School were happy to host a SEND roundtable discussion with Chipping Barnet MP and colleagues and local Headteacher and SENCO's. We discussed the implications of the SEND White Paper and collaborated on priorities for SEND children in Barnet. Lets hope the fruit of our discussion brings change for the better.

Careers Education & Guidance
Careers Education and Guidance is promoted through class learning supported by work related activities and residential opportunities that arise across the school, or by special work experience placements with trusted partners.
We aim to establish strong links between the school, local further education colleges and training providers.
A careers adviser with a specialism in learning disabilities provides guidance for pupils from Year 8 onwards and supports their transition into further education, training or employment according to their individual circumstances.

Hearts of Oak Charity
Hearts of Oak, the school charity, through the generosity of its many donors. Hearts of Oak is a charity set up by Oak Lodge, but now with restricted funds for The Windmill School. If parents would like to support Windmill's fundraising, check the Hearts of Oak website for more fundraising ideas.
Parents can also help by shopping at Amazon
Simply click on the"SHOP NOW" Button on the Heart of Oak website here: Hearts of Oak will receive up to 3% of the purchase price of anything you buy through Amazon.
We are enormously grateful to Hearts of Oak for supporting the fundraising for the £17,000 deposit required for our new Minibus.

Music
We are enormously proud to be nominated to receive the Music Mark for our school this academic year.
We are delighted to announce that Windmill has been awarded the Music Mark of Recognition for Dedication in 2025–26 in recognition of our commitment to high-quality music education and continuous improvement we offer our pupils.
This award celebrates the hard work of pupils and staff in developing a rich, inclusive music provision where every child can enhance opportunities, enjoy and grow through music. From engaging in classroom music lessons to performing in discrete music concerts our school community has shown tremendous enthusiasm and progress this year.
We are proud to display the Music Mark certificate and logo, a testament to our dedication to enhancing musical opportunities for all.
Thank you to everyone who has contributed to our success and we look forward to continuing our musical journey together!
We continue to work with our colleagues from the Barnet Education Arts Trust for bespoke music lessons.
If any pupil wishes to learn an instrument we try to match their aspirations with our available musicians from the Barnet Education Arts Trust BEAT or their partner organisations English Folk Dance and Song Society.
Music Development Plan

Music reflects the culture and society we live in, and so the teaching and learning of music enables children to better understand the world they live in and develops curiosity for different cultures and ideas. It also plays an important part in helping children feel part of a community. We provide opportunities for all children to create, play, perform and enjoy music, to develop the skills, to appreciate a wide variety of musical forms. We promote inclusion to the Barnet Music Festival in 2023-2024 Windmill pupils participated in the Barnet Music Festival at the Arts Depot with the English Folk Society presenting their sea shanties.

Charging & Remissions
Basic Equipment
The school supplies basic writing equipment, although we do try and encourage the students to have their own pens, pencils, rulers etc.
Practical lessons
At the beginning of every term parents will be asked to make a voluntary contribution towards the cost of ingredients and materials for food technology sessions. Unfortunately if there are not enough donations to cover these costs it will be necessary to restrict the activities that your child participates in and we will be unable to allow your child to bring these items home
Educational Visits
Many of the students are regularly involved in short trips and journeys in the local area that we will continue to subsidise. However most of our half- or full-day trips to educational places of interest will only be able to go ahead if parents feel able to make a voluntary contribution towards the cost.
Visits outside school hours
The school usually subsidises these trips but it may be necessary to ask for contributions to help meet the total cost of the journey/activity if there are not enough school funds available.
Residential Visits
Parents/Carers will be informed of the total cost of any residential trip and of the charges that will need to be made in order for the trip to take place.
Breakages and damages
The school will continue to ask parents to contribute to the cost of replacement of deliberately broken, damaged, defaced or lost school property.
Remissions
If a family is in receipt of specific benefits, the school is obliged by law to waive charges for board and lodging on residential journeys. The school will always consider extending this remission to other activities that may from time to time attract a charge.
